topic: mandatory severance pay (toejikgeum) for every worker after one year
title: In Korea, Leaving a Job Pays a Month per Year

slides.headline: In Korea, leaving a job **pays a month per year.**
slides.note: It's the law, not a perk.

slides.headline: It's called **toejikgeum**
slides.body: 퇴직금, retirement pay. No contract has to mention it. A national law makes every employer owe it.

slides.headline: One year is **the line**
slides.body: Work a year or more, at 15 hours a week or more, and it's yours. Part-timers count too.

slides.headline: Any reason **you leave**
slides.body: Quit for a better job, get let go, or reach the end of a contract. The money is owed either way.

slides.headline: The math: **30 days per year**
slides.body: Your average daily pay over the last three months, times 30, times the years you worked. Overtime counts.

slides.headline: Even the tiniest shop **owes it**
slides.body: Small workplaces with under five people were added from 2010. Since 2013 they pay the full amount.

slides.headline: The **11-month** trick
slides.body: Some employers end contracts one month short of a year. Courts can count back-to-back contracts as one.

slides.headline: A year in interest on **late retirement pay**
slides.body: The employer has 14 days after your last day. After that, the unpaid amount earns 20% a year.

slides.headline: Elsewhere, severance is for layoffs. **Here, for leaving.**
slides.body: In many countries it only comes if you're let go. In Korea, a year on the job is enough.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
In Korea, every worker who stays a year gets toejikgeum when they leave: about a month's pay for each year worked.

Quit or get let go, it's the same. It's the law, not a perk.

Do you get anything like this where you work?
reply: One more: since 2022, workers under 55 usually get it paid into a personal retirement account (IRP) instead of cash, so it's harder to spend right away. It's also taxed separately and lightly. Foreign workers on a one-year job count too. Does your country make employers pay anything when you leave?
fact_check: 1·2장: 근로자퇴직급여 보장법 — 사용자는 퇴직하는 근로자에게 퇴직급여 지급 의무(퇴직금 또는 퇴직연금). 계약서 기재 여부와 무관.
3장: 계속근로기간 1년 이상, 4주 평균 1주 소정근로시간 15시간 이상(근퇴법 제4조 1항 단서). 단시간 근로자 포함.
4장: 퇴직 사유(자발적 퇴사·해고·계약 만료) 무관하게 지급.
5장: 퇴직금 = 1일 평균임금 × 30일 × 재직일수/365. 평균임금 = 퇴직 전 3개월 임금 총액 ÷ 그 기간 총일수, 연장근로수당 포함(근로기준법 제2조).
7장: 11개월 쪼개기 계약 — 대법원은 계약 사이 공백이 짧고 업무가 같으면 계속근로로 인정한 판례 다수. '항상'이 아니라 'can'으로 표기.
8장: 퇴직 후 14일 이내 지급(특별한 사정 시 합의로 연장, 근퇴법 제9조). 미지급 시 지연이자 연 20%(근로기준법 제37조, 시행령 제17조). 미지급 처벌 3년 이하 징역 또는 3천만원 이하 벌금(근퇴법 제44조).
9장: 미국은 법정 퇴직금 없음, 다수 국가는 해고 시에만 해고수당. '많은 나라'로 일반화, 특정국 단정 안 함.
댓글: 2022-04-14부터 55세 미만 퇴직급여는 원칙적으로 IRP 이전(근퇴법 제9조 2항, 예외 있음 — 'usually'). 퇴직소득세 분류과세. 외국인 근로자도 적용(E-9 출국만기보험).
